Status-6 TIL that in 1954, physicist Edward Teller presented the concept of a nuclear weapon with a theoretical yield of 10 gigatons (10 billion tons) of TNT, codenamed "Project Sundial." Its yield would have been around 200 times greater than the 50-megaton Tsar Bomba, and it was estimated that the device could ignite fires across an area the size of the country of France. Teller's proposal for the bomb shocked other attendees at the Atomic Energy Commission meeting, where the project was presented, and fellow physicist Isidor Rabi dismissed it as an "advertising stunt." The works on the weapon never advanced beyond the concept stage. (Photo illustrative, from the "Castle Bravo" test) tweet

The Council of the European Union has approved €45 billion for Kiev under a two-year program worth €90 billion, according to a Council decision. The approval was a technical step following completion of the legal arrangements for Ukraine’s core funding in 2027. The European Commission approved the allocation on October 30. Of the total, €31.7 billion is earmarked for weapons and €13.3 billion for budget support.
